newsitem.title: USA: Federal hydro dams in California running full-out.
newsitem.headline: Federal hydro dams in California running full-out.

text.p: Federally-owned hydroelectric dams in California are running full-out to make space in reservoirs for future rainfall, the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec) said Tuesday.
"We are generating at absolute maximum rates," said a spokesman at the agency's Sacramento office.
"We even coaxed a couple of project managers to bring units on line that were down for maintenance so we could utilize as much water as possible to generate power," he added.
Still, spillway flows are outdistancing turbine flows by a wide margin due to the large volume water held back during recent heavy rain and flooding, the spokesman noted.
BuRec operates 12 hydropower plants in the district comprised of California, southern Oregon and western Nevada.
Power generation capacity for the projects totals 5,000 gigawatt hours (GWh) per year.
Last year output from the federal projects reached 5,500 GWh due to above-normal precipitation.
BuRec said it is too early to tell what this year holds, but indications so far are for another wet year.
"We have to pull the reservoirs down to clear space, but the ground is still soaked," the spokesman said.
He also noted that snowpack remains well above average despite some thaw due to the heavy rain.
